precepts.text: In the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel were come out of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign, he began to build the house of the Lord.
precepts.point: The manner of the king came to pass under Solomon: he levied a tax, and the tax was men. Just as men go off to war, he sent them a month on and two months off to Lebanon, to prepare the timber and stones to build the house of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“in the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel were come out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the month Zif, which is the second month … he began to build the house of the Lord.”

That building is what the levy of Israel's men was raised for: thirty thousand men sent to Lebanon by courses to prepare the timber and stones. The king Israel asked for took their sons for his work, just as Samuel said: they would “ear his ground”, “reap his harvest”, and “make his instruments of war.”

precepts.text: After the death of Aaron's two sons the Lord charges that Aaron come not at all times into the holy place within the veil, lest he die, and that when he comes he must bring a bullock and a ram, wash his flesh in water, and put on the holy linen garments, showing that entrance into the holy place was not to be taken lightly.
precepts.point: The pattern of the house was not invented by Solomon. The Most High had already shown the fashion of the sanctuary to Moses in the mount, the cherubims, the ark, the altar of incense, and all its parts.

note.label: 1 Kings 6: Building the House of the Lord

precepts.why:
“And the Lord spake unto Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they offered before the Lord, and died”. He charged “that he come not at all times into the holy place within the vail before the mercy seat, which is upon the ark; that he die not: for I will appear in the cloud upon the mercy seat.”

When Aaron came, he had to come “with a young bullock for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering”, put on “the holy linen coat”, the linen breeches, girdle and mitre, “these are holy garments; therefore shall he wash his flesh in water, and so put them on.” Entrance into the holy place was not to be taken lightly.

The pattern of the house was not invented by Solomon. The Most High had already shown the fashion of the sanctuary to Moses in the mount: the holy place within the vail, the mercy seat upon the ark, and all its parts. Solomon spent seven years building the house “according to all the fashion of it”, the fashion the Most High had given.

precepts.text: Solomon carved all the walls of the house round about with carved figures of cherubims, palm trees, and open flowers.
precepts.point: He made the most holy house twenty cubits long and twenty broad, overlaid with fine gold to the amount of six hundred talents, and the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He overlaid the upper chambers also with gold.
precepts.why:
Kings gives the fuller picture of the walls: “he carved all the walls of the house round about with carved figures of cherubims and palm trees and open flowers, within and without.” That is what Chronicles means when it says he “graved cherubims on the walls”.

Solomon cieled the greater house “with fir tree, which he overlaid with fine gold, and set thereon palm trees and chains.” He “garnished the house with precious stones for beauty: and the gold was gold of Parvaim.” He overlaid “the house, the beams, the posts, and the walls thereof, and the doors thereof, with gold”, real gold through and through, not the counterfeit metal of today.

So the house of the Lord itself was carved round about with figures, by the king who built it for the Most High. Solomon was not bowing down to the cherubims and images he made.

points: In the four hundred and eightieth year after Israel came out of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign, in the month Zif, he begins to build the house of the Lord. That span reaches back through the time of the judges and the reign of Saul and David, a long stretch in which Israel had no settled kingly rule until this point.

note.label: 1 Kings 6: Building the House of the Lord

points: The house is threescore cubits long, twenty broad, and thirty high, with a porch of twenty cubits before it, and windows of narrow lights, the kind of angled skylights that bring light in from above.

note.label: 1 Kings 6: Building the House of the Lord

points: Against the wall of the house Solomon builds chambers round about, the lowest five cubits broad, the middle six, and the third seven, with rests in the wall so the beams need not be fastened into it. Stairs wound up from the middle chamber into the third.

note.label: 1 Kings 6: Building the House of the Lord

points: The house was built of stone made ready before it was brought, so that no hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron was heard while it was in building. Everything was hewn and fitted beforehand and set together on site, and the whole was covered with beams and boards of cedar.

note.label: 1 Kings 6: Building the House of the Lord

points: The word of the Lord comes to Solomon concerning the house, that if he walks in the statutes, executes the judgments, and keeps the commandments, the Most High will perform the word he spoke to David and will dwell among the children of Israel and not forsake his people. Solomon builds the house and finishes it.

note.label: 1 Kings 6: Building the House of the Lord

points: Solomon lines the walls within with boards of cedar from floor to ceiling and covers the floor with planks of fir, and the cedar within is carved with knops and open flowers so that no stone is seen inside. He prepares the oracle, the most holy place, to set there the ark of the covenant, twenty cubits every way, and overlays it with pure gold.

note.label: 1 Kings 6: Building the House of the Lord

points: He overlays the whole house within with gold until all is finished, the altar of cedar also covered, with a partition of gold chains before the oracle. The inside was pure gold everywhere, fit for the King, though Solomon himself confessed that the heaven of heavens cannot contain the Most High, yet this is what was made for him to dwell in while on the earth.

note.label: 1 Kings 6: Building the House of the Lord

points: Within the oracle Solomon makes two cherubims of olive tree, each ten cubits high, each wing five cubits, so that the wings reach ten cubits from tip to tip. The two cherubims are of one measure and size, set in the inner house so that one wing of each touches a wall and the other wing touches the other cherub's wing in the midst of the house, over the place of the ark.

note.label: 1 Kings 6: Building the House of the Lord

points: He overlays the cherubims with gold and carves all the walls round about with figures of cherubims, palm trees, and open flowers, within and without, and overlays the floor with gold. This is scriptural proof that images were made inside the house where the Most High dwelt.

note.label: 1 Kings 6: Building the House of the Lord

points: The fourth part and fifth part describe the framing of the doorway, the trim set frame within frame, the folding doors sliding open into the holy place and the most holy place.

note.label: 1 Kings 6: Building the House of the Lord

points: For the entering of the oracle he makes doors of olive tree, the side posts a fifth part of the wall, carved with cherubims, palm trees, and open flowers and overlaid with gold. For the door of the temple he makes posts of olive tree a fourth part of the wall, the doors of fir folding open in two leaves each, carved and covered with gold.

note.label: 1 Kings 6: Building the House of the Lord

points: Solomon builds the inner court with three rows of hewn stone and a row of cedar beams. The foundation is laid in the month Zif of the fourth year, and the house is finished throughout in the month Bul, the eighth month of the eleventh year, so he was seven years in building it.

The pattern of the house was not invented by Solomon. The Most High had already shown the fashion of the sanctuary to Moses in the mount, the cherubims, the ark, the altar of incense, and all its parts.
